summary: Defines a Management Information Base (MIB) module with managed objects for the Fabric Address Manager of a Fibre Channel network. Network management tools can use it to monitor how addresses are handed out. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: Think of a hotel desk that hands out room numbers. This document lets a monitoring tool look at how that desk is doing its job.

subtitle: SNMP objects for watching and nudging how a Fibre Channel fabric hands out Domain_IDs and addresses.

tldr.problem: Fibre Channel switches acquire Domain_IDs and manage address identifiers, but there was no standard SNMP way to see or configure that work.
tldr.mechanism: The T11-FC-FABRIC-ADDR-MGR-MIB module defines groups for per-switch settings, the domain database, assigned areas, a cache of released addresses, fabric reconfiguration commands and notifications. A second module, T11-TC-MIB, supplies shared textual conventions.
tldr.outcome: Managers can read domain and address state in a uniform way and, with care, request a fabric reconfiguration. It is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

today: RFC 4439 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2006, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. Its companion RFC 4438 reuses the T11-TC-MIB conventions defined here.

sections.title: What the Fabric Address Manager MIB Covers
sections.content:
RFC 4439 defines managed objects for a Fibre Channel network's Fabric Address Manager. That term refers to acquiring Domain_IDs as specified in FC-SW-3 and managing Fibre Channel identifiers as specified in FC-FS.

The document contains two MIB modules: T11-FC-FABRIC-ADDR-MGR-MIB, and T11-TC-MIB, which defines textual conventions that other T11 MIBs may also use. It extends the FC Management MIB (RFC 4044), which replaces the first FC MIB, RFC 2837, to cover domains and addresses within a domain.
sections.eli5: It is a rulebook for reading the log of who gave out which numbers in a big storage network.

sections.title: Domains and Address Identifiers
sections.content:
Fibre Channel frames carry 24-bit address identifiers for source and destination ports. In a fabric a switch assigns them dynamically. Each octet is one level of an address hierarchy, with the Domain_ID at the top.

Each switch gets one or more unique Domain_IDs in two steps. First one switch is selected as the Principal Switch. Then the Principal Switch assigns Domain_IDs to the other switches. Address assignment inside a domain is done by the switch that was granted that Domain_ID.
sections.eli5: One captain is picked, and the captain gives every switch its own street number. Each switch then numbers the houses on its own street.

sections.title: Indexes and Groups
sections.content:
Objects are indexed by the management instance (fcmInstanceIndex), the switch (fcmSwitchIndex) and a Fabric Index (t11FamFabricIndex). The Fabric Index exists because FC-SW-4 supports multiple Virtual Fabrics; in a fabric conformant to FC-SW-3 it is always 1. The switch index is listed before the fabric index so a query about all fabrics a switch is connected to is simple. The Fabric Index textual convention has a range of 0 to 4095.

The MIB has six groups:

  • t11FamGroup: basic Fabric Address Manager information per switch, including per-interface configuration.
  • t11FamDatabaseGroup: which switches are assigned to which domains.
  • t11FamAreaGroup: which Port-IDs have been assigned within the areas of the local domain.
  • t11FamCacheGroup (conditionally mandatory): recently released address assignments, kept so a best-effort attempt can reassign the same identifiers for a Preferred Domain_ID.
  • t11FamCommandGroup (optional): objects that start an operation on a Fabric.
  • t11FamNotificationGroup: notifications of significant events.
sections.eli5: The information is sorted into six drawers: switch settings, the list of domains, the numbered areas, a box of recently returned numbers, a button panel and an alarm bell.

sections.title: Configuring the Domain_ID
sections.content:
The read-write object t11FamConfigDomainId holds a switch's configured Domain_ID, with its meaning set by t11FamConfigDomainIdType, which defaults to preferred. A switch asks the Principal Switch for the configured value with an RDI (Request Domain_ID).

  • preferred: valid values are 0 to 239, and 0 means any. If the value cannot be assigned, any other Domain_ID is acceptable.
  • insistent: valid values are 1 to 239. If it cannot be granted, no other Domain_ID is acceptable.
  • static: valid values are 1 to 239. There is no Principal Switch in the Fabric, and the value is assigned by configuration together with the Fabric_Name.

If a preferred value cannot be granted at all, or an insistent value is refused, that is an error: the switch isolates its E_Ports on that Fabric and the administrator is informed through a notification. A switch with a static Domain_ID replies to EFP, BF, RCF, DIA or RDI with an SW_RJT and isolates the receiving E_Port.
sections.eli5: You can tell a switch which street number you would like. It can be a wish, a firm demand, or a fixed assignment with no captain involved.

sections.title: Reconfiguration Requests and Notifications
sections.content:
FC-SW-3 warns that Reconfigure Fabric (RCF) causes a complete reconfiguration and may change addresses, so it should be used with caution. Build Fabric (BF) attempts reconfiguration without losing or changing addresses and should be tried first. FC-MI forbids a Fabric from autonomously generating an RCF but allows an outside administrative function to ask a switch to generate one.

The MIB fits this through t11FamAutoReconfigure and t11FamRestart, both read-write. Setting t11FamRestart to disruptive generates an RCF, nonDisruptive generates a BF, and noOp does nothing; reading it always returns noOp. The compliance section requires only read-only support for these two objects. A successful SET only requests the action; SNMP cannot ensure the SW_ILS operation succeeds.

Three notifications exist: t11FamDomainIdNotAssignedNotify, t11FamNewPrincipalSwitchNotify and t11FamFabricChangeNotify. The last is sent when a switch sends or receives a BF or RCF on a Fabric. The new-principal notice is sent upon expiration of a selection timer equal to twice F_S_TOV.
sections.eli5: There is a big reset button and a gentle reset button. The rulebook says try the gentle one first, because the big one can make everyone change numbers.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Several objects are writable and sensitive. The RFC lists those that change the address allocation policy (t11FamConfigDomainId, t11FamConfigDomainIdType, t11FamContiguousAllocation), those that can cause a fabric reconfiguration (t11FamRestart, t11FamAutoReconfigure), t11FamPriority (which affects the Principal Switch), t11FamRcFabricNotifyEnable, t11FamIfRcfReject and t11FamIfRowStatus.

Readable tables holding configuration, status or assigned and recently released addresses may also be sensitive. Versions of SNMP before SNMPv3 lack adequate security. The RFC RECOMMENDS SNMPv3 with cryptographic security and says deploying older versions is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: Some buttons can shake up the whole network, so only trusted people should get to press them.

items.label: preferred
items.desc: Values 0 to 239; another Domain_ID is acceptable if this one is unavailable.

items.label: insistent
items.desc: Values 1 to 239; no other Domain_ID is acceptable.

items.label: static
items.desc: Values 1 to 239; assigned by configuration, with no Principal Switch.
